dataset.scope: India national baseline — 2W and 4W passenger (LMV) only
dataset.note: Educational summaries. Penalty amounts follow Central notifications and may change; verify locally.

entries.title: Helmet for rider and pillion
entries.simple_rule: Every person riding a two-wheeler must wear protective headgear of the type prescribed by the Central Government, unless a specific statutory exception applies.
should_do: Wear a BIS-compliant helmet with strap fastened before moving.
Ensure the pillion also wears a helmet unless a notified exception applies.
Replace damaged or expired helmets.
should_not_do: Ride without a helmet or with the strap unfastened.
Carry a pillion without headgear where required.
Use non-standard or decorative headgear that is not approved.
entries.penalty: Offence under MVA s.194D — compounding fine as per current notification (commonly ₹1,000 for first offence; higher for repeat offences). Disqualification may apply in aggravated cases.

entries.title: Seat belt for driver and front-seat passengers
entries.simple_rule: Drivers and passengers in the front seats of a motor vehicle must wear seat belts where the vehicle is equipped with them, subject to notified exceptions.
should_do: Buckle up before starting the engine.
Ensure all front-seat occupants are belted.
Adjust the belt across chest and lap, not behind the back.
should_not_do: Drive with an unbelted front passenger.
Tuck the belt under the arm or behind the seat.
Disable or remove mandatory seat belts.
entries.penalty: Offence under MVA s.194B — fine as per current Central notification (commonly ₹1,000 for first offence).

entries.title: Child restraint in private car
entries.simple_rule: Children must use prescribed seat belts or child restraint systems suitable for age, height and weight where the law requires it.
entries.legal_reference: MVA s.194B; CMVR (child restraint / safety belt provisions)
should_do: Use an age-appropriate rear-facing or booster seat.
Install restraints as per manufacturer and CMVR guidance.
Keep children in the rear seat when possible.
should_not_do: Hold a child on the lap instead of using a restraint.
Allow under-age children in the front seat with airbag without proper restraint.
Use expired or damaged child seats.
entries.penalty: Offence under MVA s.194B — fine as per current notification; repeat offences may attract higher penalties.

entries.title: Valid licence for vehicle class
entries.simple_rule: No person shall drive a motor vehicle unless they hold an effective driving licence authorising that class of vehicle.
entries.legal_reference: MVA s.3 (necessity of driving licence); s.181 (penalty for driving without licence)
should_do: Carry a valid DL for the class you are driving (MCWG for geared two-wheeler, LMV for car).
Renew before expiry; apply for duplicate if lost.
Learners must display ‘L’ and follow learner conditions.
should_not_do: Drive with an expired, suspended or wrong-class licence.
Allow an unlicensed person to drive your vehicle.
Use a learner licence without a qualified supervisor where required.
entries.penalty: MVA s.181 — fine up to ₹5,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 months for first offence; higher for repeat offences.

entries.title: Learner licence conditions (two-wheeler / car)
entries.simple_rule: A learner must follow prescribed conditions including supervision, learner plate display and restrictions on certain roads or times where notified.
should_do: Display ‘L’ sign as prescribed.
Ride/drive only with a qualified supervisor where required.
Follow any State/UT learner restrictions.
should_not_do: Carry pillion on a learner two-wheeler where prohibited.
Drive on highways or notified routes barred for learners.
Practice without the required supervisor.
entries.penalty: Breaching learner conditions is an offence under MVA/CMVR — fine and possible cancellation of learner licence.

entries.title: Mandatory third-party insurance
entries.simple_rule: Every motor vehicle using public roads must have valid third-party insurance as required by law.
should_do: Renew insurance before expiry.
Keep certificate or digital proof accessible.
Transfer insurance promptly when buying a used vehicle.
should_not_do: Drive with lapsed or fake insurance.
Alter insurance documents.
Ignore insurer intimation after an accident.
entries.penalty: MVA s.196 — fine up to ₹2,000 or imprisonment up to 3 months (first offence); higher for repeat offences.

entries.title: Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate
entries.simple_rule: Motor vehicles must carry a valid PUC certificate showing emissions within prescribed limits.
entries.legal_reference: CMVR (emission norms); MVA s.190 (general penalty for contraventions)
should_do: Test emissions at an authorised centre before expiry.
Service the vehicle if it fails the test.
Keep the PUC certificate in the vehicle or digital form.
should_not_do: Drive with an expired or missing PUC.
Tamper with the exhaust or catalytic system.
Use fake PUC certificates.
entries.penalty: Fine under MVA s.190 and CMVR — commonly ₹1,000 to ₹2,000; vehicle may be detained until compliance.

entries.title: Registration certificate (RC) and number plate
entries.simple_rule: A vehicle must be registered and display the assigned registration mark in the prescribed form and place.
should_do: Carry RC (physical or DigiLocker/mParivahan).
Use prescribed size, font and HSRP where notified.
Update address or ownership through RTO promptly.
should_not_do: Drive an unregistered or temporarily misused vehicle beyond allowed period.
Use fancy, unreadable or obscured plates.
Display a different number or borrowed plates.
entries.penalty: MVA ss.39/50 offences — fine and possible seizure; using false plates is a serious offence.

entries.title: Dangerous or rash driving
entries.simple_rule: No person shall drive dangerously or in a manner that puts others at risk, including racing, stunting or grossly negligent riding/driving.
should_do: Match speed to road, traffic and weather.
Keep both hands on controls; stay in lane.
Slow down near schools, junctions and pedestrians.
should_not_do: Perform stunts, wheelies or street racing.
Weave through traffic at high speed.
Overtake on blind curves or junctions.
entries.penalty: MVA s.184 — fine up to ₹5,000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months (first offence); licence may be suspended.

entries.title: Drunk driving / substance impairment
entries.simple_rule: Driving or riding with blood-alcohol above the prescribed limit, or under the influence of drugs, is prohibited.
should_do: Use a sober driver or taxi after consuming alcohol.
Wait until fully fit before riding/driving.
Cooperate with lawful breath/blood tests.
should_not_do: Drive after drinking even ‘a little’.
Refuse lawful testing by authorised personnel.
Mix medicines that impair reaction time and then drive.
entries.penalty: MVA s.185 — fine up to ₹10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months (first offence); higher and licence seizure for repeat offences.

entries.title: Mobile phone while driving
entries.simple_rule: Using a handheld mobile phone while driving or riding, in a way that causes danger or distraction, is treated as dangerous driving.
entries.legal_reference: MVA s.184; CMVR / court interpretations on mobile use
should_do: Stop at a safe place to take calls or navigate.
Use hands-free only where it does not distract.
Set music/maps before moving off.
should_not_do: Text, scroll or watch video while moving.
Hold the phone to the ear in slow traffic without hands-free.
Live-stream or vlog while riding/driving.
entries.penalty: Treated as dangerous driving under MVA s.184 — fine up to ₹5,000 and possible licence action.

entries.title: Parking and stopping restrictions
entries.simple_rule: You must not stop or park where signs, markings or local rules prohibit it, or where it blocks traffic, crossings or emergency access.
should_do: Use marked bays and pay fees where required.
Stop only briefly at kerb if picking up/dropping off where allowed.
Keep zebra crossings, bus stops and junctions clear.
should_not_do: Park on footpaths, flyovers or medians.
Block driveways, hydrants or hospital entrances.
Leave the vehicle on a no-parking sign stretch.
entries.penalty: Fine under MVA s.122 / local bylaws — commonly ₹500–₹2,000; towing and detention possible.

entries.title: Jumping red light / ignoring signal
entries.simple_rule: Drivers and riders must obey traffic signals. Entering the junction on red when required to stop is an offence.
entries.legal_reference: MVA s.177 (general penalty); signal rules under CMVR / local traffic police
should_do: Stop at the stop line on amber if safe to do so.
Wait on red until green.
Give way to pedestrians on green where turning.
should_not_do: Accelerate on amber when you cannot clear safely.
Enter the junction when it is already blocked.
Ignore a non-working signal without treating it as an all-way caution.
entries.penalty: Fine commonly ₹1,000–₹5,000 under compounding rules; repeat offences may lead to licence suspension.

entries.title: Give way to emergency vehicles
entries.simple_rule: Give free passage to fire service, ambulance and other notified emergency vehicles with active siren/lights.
should_do: Pull left and slow or stop safely.
Do not block junctions or gates.
Stay calm and avoid sudden U-turns.
should_not_do: Tailgate an ambulance to skip traffic.
Refuse to yield or intentionally obstruct.
Stop in the middle of the lane without clearing space.
entries.penalty: MVA s.194E — fine of ₹10,000 and possible community service for obstruction.

entries.title: Duty after an accident
entries.simple_rule: If you are involved in an accident causing injury, death or property damage, you must stop, give assistance, and report to police as required.
should_do: Stop immediately at a safe spot.
Call 112/108 for injuries; give first aid if trained.
Share identity, licence and insurance details; cooperate with police.
should_not_do: Leave the scene (hit-and-run).
Move injured persons unsafely unless fire/fuel risk.
Argue on the carriageway and block traffic.
entries.penalty: Hit-and-run and failure to report — imprisonment and fine under MVA ss.134/187; licence may be cancelled.

entries.title: Zebra crossing — pedestrian priority
entries.simple_rule: Drivers must slow down and give way to pedestrians who are crossing or waiting to cross at a marked crossing or intersection.
entries.legal_reference: MVA general duty of care; CMVR / Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations
should_do: Slow before every zebra crossing.
Stop if a pedestrian has stepped on or is clearly waiting to cross.
Make eye contact and wait until they finish.
should_not_do: Honk to force pedestrians back.
Overtake another vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian.
Block the crossing while waiting in traffic.
entries.penalty: Fine under traffic compounding rules; dangerous driving (s.184) if grossly negligent.

entries.title: Safe overtaking
entries.simple_rule: Overtake only when it is safe, legal and you have clear visibility; return to your lane without cutting in.
entries.legal_reference: CMVR / Driving Regulations 2017; MVA s.184 if dangerous
should_do: Check mirrors, signal, and blind spots.
Ensure oncoming lane is clear and no solid line prohibits crossing.
Pass with adequate gap and return smoothly.
should_not_do: Overtake on curves, crests, junctions or zebra crossings.
Overtake from the left on highways where not permitted.
Force another driver to brake or swerve.
entries.penalty: Dangerous overtaking — MVA s.184; crossing solid line may attract separate fine under local rules.

entries.title: Wrong-side / contra-flow riding
entries.simple_rule: Ride only on the correct side of the road and in the lawful direction of traffic unless directed otherwise by police.
should_do: Use the left side as per Indian rules unless overtaking.
Obey one-way signs and road markings.
Take a legal U-turn if you missed a turn.
should_not_do: Ride facing oncoming traffic to save distance.
Use footpaths or service lanes against flow.
Cut through medians illegally.
entries.penalty: Dangerous driving under MVA s.184 — fine and possible licence suspension.

entries.title: Excess passengers in private car
entries.simple_rule: Do not carry more passengers than the seating capacity stated in the registration certificate.
should_do: Check RC seating capacity (driver included in some interpretations — verify locally).
Use a second vehicle or trip for extra people.
Ensure everyone has a seat and belt where required.
should_not_do: Carry passengers in the boot or on laps beyond capacity.
Overload a hatchback with six when licensed for five.
Carry children standing between seats.
entries.penalty: MVA s.194A — fine per excess passenger as per current notification.

entries.title: Pillion rider rules (two-wheeler)
entries.simple_rule: Carry only the permitted number of pillion riders with required footrests and safety gear where the law applies.
should_do: Carry one pillion on a standard two-wheeler unless vehicle type allows otherwise.
Ensure footrests and handholds are used.
Both rider and pillion wear helmets where required.
should_not_do: Carry two or more pillion passengers (triple riding).
Carry children standing in front of the rider.
Allow pillion without foot on pegs.
entries.penalty: Fine under CMVR/MVA for overloading and helmet breaches; dangerous driving if grossly unsafe.
